newsitem.title: POLAND: MICHAEL JACKSON EYES $100 MLN PROJECT IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: MICHAEL JACKSON EYES $100 MLN PROJECT IN POLAND.

text.p: American pop star Michael Jackson, arriving in Warsaw for a two-day visit on Tuesday, is planning a major investment project in the country's capital, Polish officials said.

Jackson is hunting for a site much bigger than the Warsaw Zoo for a project whose value will exceeed $100 million, PAP news agency reported the head of Poland's State Foreign Investment Agency, Waldemar Dabrowski, as saying on Monday.

He declined to elaborate, saying it was too early to speak of details, but public television quoted unofficial sources as saying the entertainer was interested in setting up a Disneyland-style theme park in Poland.
He was also hunting about for a European residence, the television added.

"He is interested in major investments in Warsaw. This will be something magnificent, a big project which may become a great European attraction," the Polish agency quoted Warsaw Mayor Marcin Swiecicki as saying.
"Jackson's two-day visit will be economic in character, and the signing of concrete contracts is planned," the mayor added.
Upon arriving at Warsaw airport on Tuesday, Jackson will fly by helicopter over the capital to view suitable sites.
He is also due to tour an historic Warsaw landmarks and visit a children's hospital and a secondary school.
Jackson's first visit to Poland took place last September when he performed for 100,000 fans at a Warsaw airport.
